reviewer: ChatGPT-assisted development assessment; pending separate review
summary: In this 17-abstract development pool, related studies report body-fat changes, weight changes or dietary associations, but none identified in the assisted review directly establishes the exact restricted-food claim and its large, rapid fat-loss wording. Weight change is not equivalent to fat loss; observational adherence associations are not randomized diet effects. Guidance is contextual, not an experimental refutation. This is an abstract-only draft, not a final verdict or an autonomous verification result.

criteria.wording: Switching to the exact foods and beverages described in the claim, including the stated exclusions, produces body-fat loss.
criteria.rationale: The metabolic-ward study estimates fat loss under different, isocaloric dietary restrictions with daily exercise. The Paleo adherence analysis randomizes exercise conditions, not dietary adherence. The minimally processed-food trial reports weight change in its abstract. These do not establish the exact claimed dietary effect.

citations.quote: Body fat loss was calculated as the difference between daily fat intake and net fat oxidation measured while residing in a metabolic chamber.
Participants were asked to follow a Paleolithic diet for 12 weeks and were randomized to supervised exercise or general exercise recommendations.
The primary outcome was the within-participant difference in percent weight change (%WC) between diets, from baseline to week 8.

criteria.wording: The amount of body-fat loss is large, as expressed by "a lot".
criteria.rationale: The claim provides no quantitative threshold. A fat-mass percentage contrast at 12 months in a different dietary comparison cannot establish the size of fat loss under this exact diet. Do not convert this percentage contrast into kilograms or absolute fat loss.

citations.quote: fat mass (mean difference in change, -1.5% [CI, -2.6% to -0.4%]; P = 0.011)

criteria.rationale: The claim supplies no duration. A six-day metabolic-ward comparison and measurements up to 12 months describe different settings and diets. Do not invent a time cutoff or equate early weight change with rapid fat loss.

citations.quote: We selectively restricted dietary carbohydrate versus fat for 6 days following a 5-day baseline diet in 19 adults with obesity confined to a metabolic ward where they exercised daily.
Data on weight, cardiovascular risk factors, and dietary composition were collected at 0, 3, 6, and 12 months.

criteria.wording: The effect applies to people previously eating a lot of processed foods and excess carbohydrates and fats together.
criteria.rationale: One trial includes high habitual UPF intake, but tests Eatwell-guided diets and reports weight change. Other evidence includes obesity or type 2 diabetes and different interventions. This provides partial contextual overlap without establishing the full exposure, outcome and prior-diet combination.

evidence_gaps: The magnitude and duration of "a lot" and "very quickly" are unspecified; no thresholds were invented.
No direct test of the complete restricted-food and beverage claim was identified in the reviewed 17 abstracts. This is not proof that no such study exists.
Only the pooled top-10 candidates from two rankings were reviewed, not every retrieved article or the whole literature; this is not an exhaustive systematic review.
Full texts, risk of bias, study overlap and applicability have not been independently assessed.
Linked corrections 31269427 and 33027677 for 31105044, and 36183244 for 35362512, remain unchecked. No numerical effects from those sources are used in these criteria.
This assessment and its source-role judgments are assistant-assisted development work, not independent expert validation.

25178568.rationale: A 12-month randomized comparison reports fat-mass differences. Diet and timing differ from the exact claim; the percent fat-mass contrast must not be reported as kilograms or absolute fat loss.

26278052.rationale: Six-day randomized-order isocaloric feeding comparison estimates body-fat loss using fat balance. It does not test the exact food list, and does not establish the necessity of excluding grains/dairy.

28676132.rationale: Systematic review of mostly observational pediatric evidence on ultra-processed foods and body fat. Associations in children/adolescents do not establish the effect of switching to the prescribed diet.

31105044.rationale: Two-week randomized feeding comparison reports energy intake and weight in this abstract, not body-fat change. Follow linked errata before relying on numerical results; missing abstract endpoints may exist in full text.

32990607.rationale: Randomized study in NAFLD reports two-month body-fat decreases within the intervention group. A between-group fat-loss effect is not explicitly reported in the abstract. Diet includes high fiber and education and is not the exact food list.

33479499.rationale: Randomized two-week feeding periods compare energy intake. The abstract does not report a body-fat result; this is not evidence that the full study lacks one. One participant withdrew due to hypoglycemia during the low-carbohydrate diet.

33802738.rationale: Secondary analysis relates diet adherence to lower fat mass at 12 weeks in T2D. Participants were randomized to exercise conditions, not to high versus low Paleo adherence; do not treat adherence associations as randomized diet effects.

33916669.rationale: Narrative review discusses short-term fat-mass reduction and longer-term limitations of LCD. It is neither a new trial nor an exact assessment of the video diet. Safety assertions require checking underlying evidence.

34515299.rationale: Conceptual carbohydrate-insulin model with testable hypotheses; not an intervention effect estimate or established demonstration of rapid fat loss.

35362512.rationale: Mostly observational pediatric systematic review includes percentage-body-fat associations, low certainty, heterogeneous exposures. Not a trial of the prescribed diet; linked erratum requires review before using estimates.

36313106.rationale: Long-term UPF/body-composition association in a cohort, with reported associations only in women. Not rapid fat loss following randomized diet substitution.

37296485.rationale: Position statement directly useful for reviewing quick-loss promises, food-group exclusions and energy deficit. Critical guidance is relevant but not an experimental refutation of the exact claim.

37535715.rationale: Short abstract lists possible obesity drivers and discusses weight-loss drugs; it supplies no dietary fat-loss effect or focused assessment of the claimed restriction.

40760353.rationale: Eight-week minimally processed versus UPF feeding periods report weight-change outcomes. Primary endpoint is weight, not body fat in this abstract. Both diets follow Eatwell guidance and do not establish necessity of the video exclusions.

40933253.rationale: Diet comparison targets glycemia while maintaining stable weight. No fat-loss estimate is reported in the abstract. Stable weight must not be interpreted as proof of zero body-fat change.

41628734.rationale: Cancer nutrition review does not evaluate whether the prescribed restriction produces rapid body-fat loss. Shared food vocabulary is insufficient.

42502137.rationale: MASLD lifestyle overview concerns weight management and hepatic disease. It reports no evaluation of rapid whole-body fat loss from the exact restriction in the abstract.
